{{short description|Canadian mathematics educator}}
{{use dmy dates|cs1-dates=ly|date=July 2020}}
'''Jill E. Britton''' (6 November 1944 – 29 February 2016) was a Canadian [[mathematics education|mathematics educator]] known for her educational books about mathematics.

==Career==
Britton was born on 6 November 1944. She taught for many years, at [[Dawson College]] in [[Westmount, Quebec]],{{r|obit}} moving in the late 1980s to [[Camosun College]] in [[Victoria, British Columbia]].{{r|obit|camosun}} At Camosun, she taught mathematics mainly to young women aiming to become elementary school teachers. Her own teaching had the goal of changing these students' attitude about mathematics from fear to enthusiasm.{{r|camosun}} She retired in 2015, and died on 29 February 2016.{{r|obit}}

==Publications==
Britton was the author of mathematics books including:
*''Introduction to Tessellations'' (with Dale Seymour, Dale Seymour Publications, 1989){{r|intro}}
*''Tessellation Teaching Masters'' (with Dale Seymour, Dale Seymour Publications, 1989){{r|intro}}
*''Teaching Tessellating Art: Activities and Transparency Masters'' (with Walter Britton, Dale Seymour Publications, 1992){{r|tta}}
*''Explorations with Tesselmania! Activities for Math and Art Classrooms'' (Dale Seymour Publications, 1997){{r|xt}}
*''Investigating Patterns: Symmetry and Tessellations'' (Dale Seymour Publications, 2000){{r|ip}}
*''Polyhedra Pastimes'' (Dale Seymour Publications, 2001){{r|pp}}

She was also known for her "spectacular web site on symmetry and tessellations".{{r|focus}}

==Recognition==
Britton was the 2008–2009 winner of the Teaching Excellence Award of the [[Colleges and Institutes Canada|Association of Canadian Community Colleges]].{{r|accc}}
